72723.subject: Agricultural Science
72723.question_text:
(a) Mention 3 ways each by which the following agricultural programmes and institute have contributed to agricultural development in West Africa:

  i   cooperative farming

  ii  farm settlement scheme

  iii  agricultural research institute

 (b) Name one tractor-mounted implement each that would perform a similar function as as the following farm tools.

      (i) Dibber: (ii) Hoe  (iii) Sickle  (iv) Wheelbarrow (v) Watering can: 

 (c) State two:

       (i) advantages of using the mouldboard plough;

       (ii) disadvantages of using the mouldboard plough.
72723.explanation:
(a) Ways by which the following agricultural programmes sand institute has contributed to the agricultural development in West Africa.

(ii) Cooperative farming:

   -  Farmers pool their resources to obtain credit facilities at low interest rates

   -  The cooperative helps farmers to store farm produce to the market 

   -   Facilitates joint processing of produce

(ii) Farm Settlement scheme

    -  Reduces unemployment among youths

    -  Helps to make agriculture attractive to youths

    -  Settlers are taught improved farming techniques

    -  Improves agricultural productivity

    -  Helps in developing rural areas/provision for basic amenities

 (iii) Agricultural research institute develops 

     -  New varieties of crops and breeds of animals 

     -  Better methods of controlling pests and diseases

     -  Breeds of animals and varieties of crops that are resistant to pests and diseases

     -  Better storage and processing facilities

     -  New cultural practices and better farming systems for greater yield.

(b) Tractor mounted implement that could perform similar functions as the following farm tools

 (i)    Dibber

      - Seed drill/planter/combine/ drill

 (ii)    Hoe

      - i Plough  ii Harrow  iii Ridger  iv Cultivator 

 (iii)    Sickle

      -  Mower/Slasher 

     -  Harvester

 (iv)   Wheel barrow

      -  Trailer/cart/wagon

      -   Bucket loader

  (v)   Watering Can

      -  Boom sprayer

      -  Sprinkler irrigation system

   c (i)  Advantages of using mould-board plough

      -    Can be used in soils free from stumps/stones

      -    Shares can be resharpened by grinding

      -    Buries weeds/crops deeply 

      (ii)  Disadvantages of using the mould-board plough

       -    Not adapted to tropical soil with obstacles 

       -    loses its share point easily when in contact with obstacles

       -    predisposes the soil to erosion 

       -    Frequent usage leads to soil compaction/formation of hard pan

72729.subject: Agricultural Science
72729.question_text:
(a) With the aid of a pH scale,explain the term soil pH.

 b(i) What are cover crops?

   (ii) Mention five advantages of planting cover crops on farm.

   (c) Complete the table below.

 Weed        Botanical  Name
 Wild marigold  
 Spear grass  
 Stubborn grass  
 Pig weed  
 Carpet grass
72729.explanation:
(a)Explanation of the soil pH using the pH scale above.

  Soil pH is defined as a measure of the degree of alkalinity of the soil/a measure of the concentration of hydrogen ions (H+) or hydroxyl ions (OH-) in the soil.

- A pH scale is graduated from 1 - 14

- A soil whose pH is below 7 is said to be alkaline.

- A soil whose pH is above 7 is said to be acidic 

- A soil with pH 7 is said to be neutral

b(i) Meaning of Cover crops

Cover crops are crops that sre grown specifically to cover the soil and protect it from erosion and leaching for a given length of time.

  (ii) Advantages of planting cover crops

    -   Effective in controlling weeds

    -   Reduces soil temperature

    -   Cover crops help to fix nitrogen in the soil

    -   Serves as a green manure when ploughed into the soil

    -   Could be harvested as food crop after harvesting the cash crop

    -   Prevents soil erosion

    -   Prevents soil compaction

    -   Improves soil structure

    -   Could serve as forage for livestock

    -  Controls pests

(c)   Completion of the table

 Wild Marigold

 Stubborn grass

 Pig weed

 Carpet grass

72732.subject: Agricultural Science
72732.question_text:
(a) Give one function of each of the following bacteria in Nitrogen cycle:

      ii Rhizobium

      ii Nitrosomonas

      iii Pseudomonas

      iv Nitrobacter

 (b)  A farmer discovered that aphids have invaded a cowpea farm.

  (ii)  State three effects of aphids on the cowpea plants.

 c(i)  Explain the term forestry.

  (ii)  Name five products that could be obtained from forests.
72732.explanation:
(i) Rhizobium

    Fixation of nitrogen in the root noddles of leguminous crops

(ii) Nitrosomonas

     Oxidation of ammonium compounds to nitrites ( NO-2)

(iii) Pseudomonas

      Reduction of soil nitrates to gaseous nitrogen/dentification

(iv) Nitrobacter

      Oxidation of nitrites to nitrates (NO-3)

b(i) Effects of aphids on Cowpea plants

      Reduces the yield

      Reduces the yield of seeds

      Reduces the germination of seeds

      Serves as vectors of diseases

      May result in death of plants 

  (ii) Cultural ways by which the farmer could control aphids on the Cowpea farm

       Planting of resistant varieties 

       Planting of insect-free seeds

       Practicing crop rotation

       Inter-planting of crops

       Completion of the table

c(i)  Explanation of forestry

      Forestry is the study and management of forests and forest resources

      Forestry is the art and science of managing trees,forests and forests products for human use.

 (ii) Products that could be obtained from the forest:

     -Bush meat,Timber wood,fuel,wood/firewood,wood pulp,honey,snail,mushroom,chewing stick.

     -Palm wine,Palmoil,Kolanut,wild fruits,bamboo,gum,latex.

     -Medicinal herbs,dye,wild vegetables,fiber,resin,bush yam.

     -Long pole,wax,wild space.

72792.subject: Agricultural Science
72792.question_text:
(a) A farmer intends to cultivate sorghum on a farmland measuring 300m by 1050m at a seed rate of 60kg per hectare.

 If sorghum requires NPK 15:15:15 fertilizer at the rate of 20kg per hectare.

 Calculate the:

 (i) area of farmland in hectares

 (ii) quantity of sorghum seeds required for planting

 (iii) quantity of fertilizer required 

b(i) State two differences between building and grafting in vegetative propagation.

  (ii) Mention four crops that could be propagated by budding.

  (c) Name two groups of farm animals each that should be fed with:

  (i)  production ration

  (ii) maintenance ration
72792.explanation:
(i) Area of farmland  = length × Breadth 

                             = 300m  × 150m 

                             = 45,000 m²

Iha = 10,000 m²

Area of farm land    = 45,000 m² ÷ 10,000 m²

                                   = 4.5 ha

(ii)  Quantity of sorghum seeds required for planting 

      seed rate  =  60kg/ha 

      quantity of seeds required

      = 4.5 ha × 60kg/ha

      = 270kg

  (iii) Quantity of fertilizer required

        Fertilizer rate = 20 kg/ha

        quantity of fertilizer required 

       = 4.5 ha × 20kg/ha

       = 90kg

   b(i) Differences between pudding and grafting in vegetative propagation

                     Budding                             Grafting
Small bud is used as scion Part of a stem/branch is used as scion
A T-shaped or inverted T-shaped cut is commonly made on the stock. A slant or V-shaped is commonly made on both the stock and scion.
Commonly done during the active growing season of the stock. Usually performed when the rock is dormant e.g during harmattan.
The stock and scion does not need to   need to be of the same age and size for successful budding.

The stock and scion should be of approximately the same page and size for successful grafting.
The scion is small The scion is large

(ii) Crops that could be propagated by budding

     - Citrus/named citrus,cherry,cashew,avocado pear,mango,almond.

     -  Cocoa apple,ornamental plants,rubber,tea,peach.

 

 (c)  Groups of animals that should be fed with different types of ration 

  (i)   Production ration:

      -  Pregnant animals,weaned animals,broilers,new born animals,layers.

      -  Broilers,New born animals,layers,breeding males/females,fatteners.

      -  Growers,wool producing sheep,beef cattle,Dairy cow./low lactating animals

    (ii)  Maintenance ration:

       - Spent layers,old animals,culled animals,Dry cows,Non-lactaitng animals - non breeders

72807.subject: Agricultural Science
72807.question_text:
(a) Give two reasons each for carrying out the following practice in fish ponds:

(i)  Removal of excessive vegetation

(ii) Removal of salt

(iii) Supplematary feeding

(iv) Fertilizer application

(b) Mention five conditions that could necessitate culling of animals

(c) State five effects of excess nitrogen in soil on crops.
72807.explanation:
(a) Reasons for carrying out the following management practices in fish ponds

(i) Removal of excessive vegetation

-   Allows sunlight to reach the bottom of the pond for the growth of phytoplankton

-   Prevents breeding of fish pests

-   Ensures adequate supply of dissolved oxygen

-   Prevents breeding of fish diseases

 (ii) Removal of salt

-     Makes the pond water to be clear/reduces turbidity of pond water

-     Facilitates free movement of fish

-     Maintains normal depth of the pond

-     Ensures adequate supply of dissolved oxygen

 (iii) Supplementary Feeding

 -      Promotes rapid growth of fish

 -      Improves the health of fish

 -      Provides variety of feeds to fish/balanced diet adequate nutrition

(iv)  Fertilizer Application

-      Encourages the growth of phytoplankton

-      Provides nutrient to fish   

-      Improves the growth of fish in ponds

(b)   Conditions that could necessitate culling of farm animals

-     Low productivity/poor feed conversion

-     Old age aggressiveness

-     Lameness parturition problem

-     Diseases severe injury

-     Egg pecking/sucking

-     Poor mothering/piglet eating

-     Reproductive failure/sterility

-     Cannibalism

(c)  Effects of excess nitrogen in the soil on crops

-     Causes excessive vegetative growth 

-     Decreases reproductive growth/delay fruiting

-     Weakens plant sterns

-     Causes lodging in crops

-     Reduces the yield of some crops

72809.subject: Agricultural Science
72809.question_text:
(a) What is agricultural insurance?

 (b) Define each of the following terms in agricultural insurance

 (i)  insurance policy 

 (ii) Insurance premium

 (c)  An agricultural extension agent organized a meeting with the groundnut farmers in a village to introduce a disease resistant variety of groundnut to them.

 (i)  State four advantages of the agricultural extension method employed by the extension agent..

 (ii)  Mention three other ways by which the information should be disseminated to the group of farmers.

 (d) Enumerate five operations involved in the processing of rice after harvesting.
72809.explanation:
(a)  Meaning of agricultural insurance

      Agricultural insurance is the policy that provides farmers with financial protection against specific risks that may arise during agricultural production.

 (b) Definition of terms in agricultural insurance

  (i)  Insurance policy

       Insurance policy is a contract/document in which the insurance company/insurer agrees to indemnify/compensate the insured/farmer against

       loses from specific risks and disasters of agricultural production.

   (ii) Insurance Premium

        Insurance premium is the amount of money that that the insured farmer pays the insurance company for an insurance policy.

   c(i) Advantages of the agricultural extension method employed by the extension agent

     -  Saves costs

     -  Saves time

     -  Enables the extension agent to reach a large number of farmers

     -  Influences reluctant farmers to try the new idea/encourages farmers to develop interest in new ideas

     -   Directs attention to group problems

     -   Encourages and trains local leaders

  (iii)    Other ways by which the information could be disseminated to the group of farmers.

           Workshop - Field - trip - Debate - symposium lecture - Demonstration - discussions - Agriculture show 

  (d)     Operations Involved in the processing of rice after harvesting

           Cleaning -  parboiling - drilling - milling/hulling -Winnowing - folishing - grading - sorting - packaging - threshing
